title: Section 311 — Robbery, or dacoity, with attempt to cause death or grievous hurt

content.overview: BNS s. 311 — Robbery, or dacoity, with attempt to cause death or grievous hurt.
content.study:
Introduction and meaning
Robbery, or dacoity, with attempt to cause death or grievous hurt. BNS restatement of IPC 397. Elements are substantially the same; cite the BNS number for offences on or after 1 July 2024. BNS restatement of IPC 397. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.
In student language: BNS s. 311 is the rule on “Robbery, or dacoity, with attempt to cause death or grievous hurt”. The section provides that if, at the time of committing robbery or dacoity, the offender uses any deadly weapon, or causes grievous hurt to any person, or attempts to cause death or grievous hurt to any person, the imprisonment with which such offender shall be punished shall not be less than seven years. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 311 exists so that “Robbery, or dacoity, with attempt to cause death or grievous hurt” has a closed legal test in Chapter XVII — Of Offences Against Property. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: Theft, snatching, extortion, robbery, dacoity, trust, cheating, mischief, trespass.

The provision in detail
311. If, at the time of committing robbery or dacoity, the offender uses any deadly weapon, or causes grievous hurt to any person, or attempts to cause death or grievous hurt to any person, the imprisonment with which such offender shall be punished shall not be less than seven years

enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 311 constitutes a key component of Chapter XVII (Of Offences against Property) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, addressing robbery, or dacoity, with attempt to cause death or grievous hurt. The provision balances personal liberty with public interest and social order. The prosecution must establish every statutory element beyond reasonable doubt: the specified actus reus, the requisite mens rea, and any relevant statutory circumstances. Modern judicial interpretation emphasizes substantive fairness, proportionality in sentencing, and adherence to constitutional safeguards. Where statutory exceptions or provisos are attached to the section, the accused must establish facts bringing the case within such provisions under evidentiary standards.
examples: Teaching example (Standard application): An individual intentionally commits acts satisfying the statutory formula of robbery, or dacoity, with attempt to cause death or grievous hurt under Section 311 without lawful authority. The individual is liable under BNS s. 311.

Teaching example (Absence of mens rea / Lawful exception): A person acts in good faith or without the requisite statutory mental element under circumstances recognized by law. The essential ingredients of Section 311 are not satisfied; no penal liability attaches.
distinctions: Section 311 vs General Attempt: Section 311 penalizes the substantive conduct specified in Chapter XVII; inchoate attempts without specific provisions fall under the general attempt provisions.
Section 311 vs Cognate Chapter Offences: Liability under Section 311 is distinguished by its specific mental threshold and the particular legal interest protected under Of Offences against Property.
problemApplication: Issue: Whether the accused is liable under BNS s. 311 for conduct relating to robbery, or dacoity, with attempt to cause death or grievous hurt.
Rule: Under BNS s. 311, liability attaches upon proof of the statutory actus reus accompanied by the requisite mens rea without lawful justification.
Application: The evidence demonstrates that the accused performed the specified act with the required state of mind, satisfying all statutory ingredients of Section 311.
Conclusion: The accused is guilty of an offence under BNS s. 311 and subject to the prescribed punishment.
